title: Surrealist founders' occult séances and Breton's 1922 article

tellings.quote: these guys from the beginning of even from before it took the name surrealism were constantly engaged in occult rituals including long seances

plain: A researcher and writer, Jason Jorjani, told a podcast host, Jesse Michels, in 2025 that the founders of Surrealism, an art movement born in 1920s France, including André Breton, Max Ernst and Paul Éluard, were taking part in occult rituals and long séances, sessions meant to contact spirits, from the very start, even before the movement had its name. He ties this to an article Breton wrote in 1922, and if true it would mean a famous art movement grew partly out of spirit-contact practice.
